newsitem.title: KENYA: Zaire rebels reported beseiging eastern capital.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels reported beseiging eastern capital.

text.p: Rebels are beseiging the eastern Zairean capital of Kisangani -- the last stand for Kinshasa's ragged army in the area -- on three fronts and it could fall within days, a regional military source said on Wednesday.

The source, who closely monitors the war pitting Laurent Kabila's rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), said the rebels were within range of Kisangani on two axis beyond the northern town of Bafwasende.

He said the rebels, who have scored stunning military victories since they launched Africa's latest war in October, were also advancing from the town of Lubutu and were 40 km (25 miles) beyond it on their way to Kisangani.
Kisangani is the government army's operational base, the country's third largest city and a key diamond and gold trading centre.
Kabila has proclaimed Kisangani as his next target, giving army commanders until March 13 to lay down their arms.
"The city (Kisangani) is being beseiged. From the northern axis, the rebels are advancing on two fronts and are now within range of Kisangani," the source said.

"On the straight road from town of Lubutu, they are also advancing and have moved 40 kms (25 miles) beyond Lubutu. The road is good and with little or no resistance the rebels should cover the route within a very short period."
"Given all these dynamics, there is no doubt that Kisangani is threatened and its fall could come in a very short period," he said.

The source said the rebels were also gaining ground in mineral-rich Shaba province, where they hoped to link up with a Katangese guerrillas in neighbouring Angola. A second group of Katangese guerrillas, involved in the earlier Angolan war, backs the Zaire government.

"Our understanding is that the Katangese are split into two groups. One allied to Angolan rebel chief Jonas Savimbi and in support of Kinshasa and another one waiting for Kabila's forces to arrive in the region," the source said.
A Defence Ministry official in the capital Kinshasa said Kabila's guerrillas has gained more ground in the copper-producing Shaba to the south, taking the town of Kabalo with little resistance.
Kabalo is on the main railway line serving Shaba and 400 km (250 miles) south of the rail head at Kindu, which fell earlier.
The rebels say they have also captured the town of Manono, 160 km (100 miles) south of Kabalo in the heart of the province.

The rebel advance on Kisangani and in Shaba came after the fall of kindu, a key transport hub on the Zaire River and the northernmost working station on a rail line to South Africa. It also has a large airport used by the military.
Rebels flew foreign journalists to Kindu, 360 km (220 miles) north of Kabalo on Tuesday.

The capture of Kabalo and Manono would mark the rebels' first major advance in the southern province in weeks, and would place them within 500 km (300 miles) of the provincial capital Lubumbashi, the hub of Zaire's copper and cobalt industry.

Kabila says he is determined to end President Mobutu Sese Seko's 31-year rule. He has spurned international pressure for a cease-fire, insisting on direct negotiations with Mobutu. The ailing president is in France.
